To guide the course of a vessel, vehicle, aircraft etc. (by means of a device such as a rudder, paddle, or steering wheel).

examples.text: The boat steered towards the iceberg.
I steered homeward.

glosses: To guide the course of a vessel, vehicle, aircraft etc. (by means of a device such as a rudder, paddle, or steering wheel).

examples.text: I find it very difficult to steer a skateboard.
When planning the boat trip, we had completely forgotten that we needed somebody to steer.
I leap on board: no helmsman steers: I float till all is dark.

glosses: To be directed and governed; to take a direction, or course; to obey the helm.

examples.text: The boat steers easily.
Where the wind / Veers oft, as oft [a ship] so steers, and shifts her sail.

glosses: To direct a group of animals.
To maneuver or manipulate a person or group into a place or course of action.

examples.text: Hume believes that principles of association steer the imagination of artists.

glosses: To conduct oneself; to take or pursue a course of action.
To direct a conversation.
To direct or send an object into a specific place

examples.text: Sterling, who scored the winners against Croatia and the Czech Republic in the group stage, steered in Luke Shaw's cross after 75 minutes to send England's fans, with more than 40,000 inside Wembley, into wild celebrations.

glosses: A suggestion about a course of action.

examples.text: I tried to give you the steer, but I guess I didn't get it over. Everybody knew it but you.

glosses: A helmsman; a pilot.
The castrated male of cattle, especially one raised for beef production.

examples.text: He counted the cattle over and over. It diverted him to speculate as to how much weight each of the steers would probably put on by spring.

glosses: To castrate (a male calf).
A coxswain of a boat, especially of a racing crew.

examples.text: A particularly nervous boy was appointed cox, and the steering principle explained to him by Joskins. Joskins himself took stroke. He told the others that it was simple enough; all they had to do was to follow him.

glosses: To act as coxswain for.

examples.text: The physicist Stephen Hawking used to cox for a college rowing team.

examples.text: Even though Jack is a novice, he manages his team with great success.

glosses: To handle or control (a situation, job).

examples.text: The government managed the inflation very poorly.

glosses: To handle with skill, wield (a tool, weapon etc.).

examples.text: It was so much his interest to manage his Protestant subjects.

examples.text: She somehow managed to sit on the wet paint.

examples.text: It's a tough job, but I'll manage.

examples.text: "That's nice, dear!", she managed.

examples.text: [Let zephyrs] administer their tepid, genial airs.

glosses: To settle, as the estate of one who dies without a will, or whose will fails of an executor.
To give, as an oath.

examples.text: Swear […] to keep the oath that we administer.

glosses: To give (a drug, to a patient), be it orally or by any other means.

examples.text: We administered the medicine to our dog by mixing it in his food.

glosses: To cause (a patient, human or animal) to ingest (a drug), either by openly offering or through deceit.

examples.text: A noxious drug had been administered to him.

glosses: Proceeding without deviation or interruption.

examples.text: Be even and direct with me.

examples.text: He nowhere, that I know, says it in direct words.

glosses: To aim (something) at (something else).

examples.text: They directed their fire towards the men on the wall.

examples.text: He directed me to the left-hand road.

glosses: To point out to with authority; to instruct as a superior; to order.

examples.text: She directed them to leave immediately.

glosses: To address (a letter) to a particular person or place.

examples.text: [A]s I do not know where I shall be, and shall have my letters sent after me as soon as I do know, continue to direct hither.

examples.text: With a simple remote, he could control the toy truck.
